title: Email reputation scoring and team onboarding guardrails
creator: Asha Menon
description:
Problem: We continue to see noisy invite churn and a small number of org-joins backed by low-quality/bounced addresses. Existing allowlist/denylist rules are static and place heavy burden on Admins to maintain. We need a defensible system that combines automated email reputation signals, domain verification checks, and RBAC v2 constraints at team/org creation time to reduce malicious and accidental joins while preserving fast onboarding for legitimate customers.

Proposal: Implement an onboarding guardrails service that evaluates invites/joins through a policy pipeline: (1) Domain verification status (verified, corporate SSO-enabled, known personal domain), (2) Email reputation score (third-party signals + bounce history + internal abuse signals), (3) Org/team risk policy (per-org allowlist/denylist overrides, minimum admin verification, SSO enforcement flag), (4) Rate and pattern detection (throttles per-IP/email domain). The pipeline outputs an action: allow, require-vetting (manual review UI for admins), block, or require SSO enrollment. The service must emit structured audit logs that capture inputs, decision path, and actor, to feed Console and SIEM.

Design constraints and trade-offs: We want to avoid false positives that frustrate legitimate onboarding. Score thresholds default conservative; customers with Dedicated/Private tiers can set stricter defaults. RBAC v2 integration: guardrails must consult the planned team role assignment and block creation of high-privilege roles (org-admin, billing-admin) unless SSO or verified domain is present or an allowlist override exists. Audit logging should be tamper-evident and include policy version and rule ids.

Acceptance criteria:
- Guardrails evaluate every invite and org/team creation event in hosted flows and in the Console UI.
- Policy decisions written to audit log with schema: timestamp, event_id, decision, policy_version, inputs (domain_status,email_score,rate_flags), actor, remediation_action.
- Admins can configure per-org allowlist/denylist and set default action for borderline scores (manual review vs require SSO).
- RBAC v2 blocks creation of org-level privileged roles unless policy satisfied.
- Rollout behind feature flag with metrics: invite-block-rate, false-positive appeals, time-to-onboard for affected orgs.

Technical approach:
- New microservice onboarding-guardrails (stateless) with a policy engine (policy files stored in Gitops).
- Email reputation aggregator calls third-party APIs (e.g., Kickbox-like signals), caches scores for 24h, and augments with internal bounce/abuse counters from mailer service.
- Domain verification state pulled from existing domain table and SSO tenant metadata (SAML flags).
- RBAC v2 policy hook implemented in authz layer: pre-create check that queries onboarding-guardrails.
- Audit logs emitted as structured JSON to event pipeline (Kafka) with schema registry; archived to audit-retention cluster and visible in Console for admins.

Security considerations:
- Ensure PII minimization in logs: store hashed email when possible and retain raw email only in short-term debugging logs with restricted access.
- Rate-limit reputation API calls and add circuit-breaker to avoid SLO impact.
- security_review_required: true

Rollout plan:
- Stage 1 (alpha, internal): feature flag on staging orgs; sample traffic, validate logs and API usage (2 weeks).
- Stage 2 (canary): opt-in beta customers and Redwood internal orgs; monitor false positives (4 weeks).
- Stage 3 (gradual): 10% hosts -> 50% -> 100% with adjustable thresholds and per-org overrides (6 weeks).

Monitoring and metrics:
- invite_policy_decision_count by decision (allow/manual_review/block/require_sso)
- invite_block_rate and appeal_rate
- onboarding_time_median for orgs affected vs control
- audit_log_delivery_latency and error rate
comments: 2025-12-05 - Asha: Initial scoping meeting w/ PM (Ravi) and Security. Agreed to leverage existing domain verification table and RBAC v2 pre-create hook. Action: eng to draft policy schema.
2025-12-12 - Leo: PoC for email reputation aggregator running in sandbox. Using 3rd-party provider for scoring, added internal bounce counter join. Early results show 4% of invites with low score.
2026-01-06 - PM (Ravi): UX request - admins need a review queue and single-click approve/appeal flow, plus reasons exposed for blocked invites. Added to scope as sub-issue ENG-38903.
2026-01-10 - Security (Maya): Reviewed PII plan. Must hash emails in long-term audit store; raw email allowed in ephemeral logs with ACLs. Also requested policy-version provenance in logs.
2026-01-14 - Eng Lead (Priya): Decided to implement policy files as JSONNet under org-security-hardening repo; deploy via GitOps to avoid console-only changes. Will include canary flags per org.

2026-01-18 - QA: Integration test matrix added. Tests: verified domain + good score -> allow; unverified + low score -> block; verified + low score but Dedicated tier -> require manual review. QA link: https://confluence.redwood.ai/pages/ORG-guardrails-qa
